newsitem.title: UK: British divers marry on deck of sunken ship.
newsitem.headline: British divers marry on deck of sunken ship.

text.p: Two British scuba divers took the plunge in more ways than one on Saturday when they married 30 feet (10 metres) below sea level on the deck of a wrecked ship off the Scottish coast.
Wendy Dusberry and Eddie Benson pledged undying love on the SS Breda, sunk in World War Two, while a television camera relayed pictures of the ceremony to 50 guests on board a boat above the wreck.
The couple, who met last year during a diving holiday to the wreck, were taking advantage of changes in the law widening the places where people can get married.
"Some people might think it was daft. But Eddie and I both love diving and we wanted to get married where we met," said Wendy, who like her new husband is 30 years old.

Communications equipment linked the couple to priest Alex Kerr, who spent three months learning to dive so he could conduct the submarine ceremony. "I believe this is the first underwater wedding in Britain and it is probably the oddest one I will ever get involved in," he said afterwards.
The marriage licence lists the site of the wedding as a compass point three miles (five km) out of Ardmucknish Bay near Oban, in northwest Scotland.
